title: How a Rocket Engine Works in 60 Seconds 🚀🔥 #shorts
description:
Rocket exhaust can leave the nozzle at up to 4.5 kilometers per second. A rocket carries its own oxidizer, pumps it with fuel into a combustion chamber, and squeezes the hot gas through a narrow throat and a widening nozzle to go supersonic. Cold propellant flowing around the walls keeps the engine from melting. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#rocket #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Rocket exhaust can blast out at up to *4.5 kilometers per second*. That's about 13 times the speed of sound.

steps.label: Oxidizer
steps.text: Space has no air to burn, so a rocket carries its *own oxidizer*, like liquid oxygen, next to its fuel.

steps.label: Pumps
steps.text: Powerful *turbopumps* force the fuel and oxygen into the combustion chamber.

steps.label: Burn
steps.text: There they *ignite* and turn into extremely hot, high-pressure gas.

steps.label: Nozzle
steps.text: The gas squeezes through a narrow *throat*, hits the speed of sound, then speeds up even more as the *nozzle* widens.

steps.label: Cooling
steps.text: To survive the heat, cold propellant first flows through *channels* in the nozzle walls before it burns.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pump, burn, *blast*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
